The conversion of glucose to pyruvate occurs during glycolysis.  
In glycolysis, one glucose molecule yields two ATP molecules (net gain) and two pyruvate molecules, along with two NADH molecules.  
Water is produced in later stages (like oxidative phosphorylation), not net in glycolysis.  
The 38 ATP figure refers to total ATP yield from complete glucose oxidation (through glycolysis, Krebs cycle, and oxidative phosphorylation), not just to pyruvate.  

Final answer: (B)
